text.p: Albanian first division soccer, suspended in February because of civil unrest, resumed in four towns on Saturday after the government guaranteed adequate security in the stadiums.
In a morning match, Partizani beat Vllaznia of Shkoder 2-1 in their home stadium in the capital Tirana.
However the daily Dita Informacion newspaper reported that Lushnja in southern Albania, the area worst hit by unrest and armed banditry, would boycott the league.

The Balkan country's civil unrest, sparked by the collapse of fraudulent pyramid investment schemes in which many Albanians lost life savings, left Lushnja with heavy financial losses and a badly damaged stadium.

Five days of fixtures from the 1996/97 season have still to be played and officials said they will be held in the towns of Tirana, Kavaje, Durres and Elbasan over the next two weeks. The new season will then start on September 13.
Although the league was formally suspended in February, no matches have been played since December 29.
Flamurtari from the southern town of Vlore, the centre of the armed unrest, lead the suspended standings on 37 points followed by Tirana on 34 and Vllaznia on 33.

European soccer's governing body UEFA have suspended Albanian clubs from participating in 1997-98 Cup competitions but the national side will play a home September 10 World Cup group nine qualifier against Northern Ireland in Spain.
